item.title: The Asia-Pacific is a realm for shared devt, a stage for co-op side by side: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19 00:34:00
The APEC "China Year" logo decoration is seen at Qianhai Stone Park in Shenzhen. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday delivered a keynote speech titled "Forging Ahead with Resolve, Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific" at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province. In the speech, the Chinese leader provided an in-depth explanation of the right path for the Asia-Pacific region to navigate the profound global changes unseen in a century, and clearly outlined the vast opportunities for cooperation that China's 15th Five-Year Plan will bring to the Asia-Pacific and the world. The address drew an enthusiastic response; attendees noted that it charted a course toward shared prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and further bolstered the confidence of the region's business community in achieving mutually beneficial cooperation. The Asia-Pacific is the most dynamic region in the global economy and a primary engine of growth, as well as a hub for innovation and openness. At present, the international landscape is fraught with turbulence and complexity; global economic growth lacks sufficient momentum, while unilateralism and protectionism are on the rise. Meanwhile, global trade has demonstrated resilience despite these headwinds, and breakthroughs in emerging technologies - such as artificial intelligence and green, low-carbon solutions - are accelerating, profoundly reshaping the global division of labor and the landscape of world development. What has happened to the world, and what path should the Asia-Pacific take? Should we choose openness or closure, cooperation or fragmentation, change or stagnation? The eyes of the world are turned toward the Asia-Pacific, and the region's expectations are focused on China. China has put forward four proposals for building an Asia-Pacific community and fostering shared prosperity in the region: uphold peace and stability, build bridges of opening up and cooperation, boost innovation to drive growth, and expand our ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. These four proposals represent the "right choice" for the Asia-Pacific as it navigates a period of profound changes unseen in a century. They are grounded in the practical needs of the region's current stage of development while aligning with the long-term trajectory of global economic transformation, effectively charting a clear, reliable course for all parties in the Asia-Pacific to follow amid turbulent times. Within this substantial agenda, the opening-up dividends unleashed by China's 15th Five-Year Plan present a significant opportunity that has captured the attention of the Asia-Pacific region and the world at large. China is the world's second-largest consumer market and home to the world's largest middle-income group. Ranging from the semi-conductor, the new-energy vehicle sector and biomedicine to the broad expansion of emerging fields such as smart home technology, the silver economy and winter sports tourism, the comprehensive expansion of China's high-tech and high-value-added sectors creates brand-new opportunities for high-quality goods and services from economies across the Asia-Pacific. Through measures such as the steady reduction of tariffs, the expansion of market access, and ongoing, in-depth exploration of "institutional opening-up" - encompassing rules, regulations, management, and standards - China is fostering a more stable and predictable environment for global enterprises to invest and thrive. Regardless of how the international landscape may shift, China's commitment to mutually beneficial cooperation with the world remains steadfast. The Shenzhen initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026, released during the summit, marks the first time in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit that an outcome document has been issued in the form of an initiative. From deepening an open regional economy to driving inclusive growth through technological innovation, and from streamlining the arteries of regional integration to working together toward shared prosperity - these four priority areas outline the collective aspirations of the Asia-Pacific business community for regional cooperation, while offering a fresh approach to collaboration amidst a complex and ever-changing international economic landscape. The world is focused on Shenzhen, where a series of significant meetings are unfolding, and long-gestating cooperative concepts are being transformed into actionable, implementable plans. Inside and outside the venue, political and business leaders from the Asia-Pacific region and beyond are gathering to discuss pressing issues - such as connectivity, artificial intelligence, sustainable development, the construction of the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, and the digital economy - sharing their perspectives and proposing concrete, practical solutions. Many corporate representatives arrived with carefully prepared lists of potential collaborations, utilizing even their coffee breaks for multiple rounds of engagement to swiftly identify new partnership opportunities. Standing at a new starting point for Asia-Pacific cooperation, the coastal city of Shenzhen is fully leveraging its role as a pivotal platform for fostering consensus and pooling collective strength. APEC emerged alongside the wave of economic globalization, propelling the Asia-Pacific region to the forefront of the times. Every step forward in Asia-Pacific cooperation has been driven by a firm commitment from all parties to work together side by side. The consensus reached today in Shenzhen marks a fresh departure point for the Asia-Pacific region to navigate through storms and challenges together. As the proposals put forward and the commitments made during this meeting are translated into concrete action, the vision and blueprint for an Asia-Pacific community will gradually become a reality of common prosperity, infusing a vital sense of certainty into an otherwise turbulent and unsettled world.

item.title: GT Voice: Can China's chips power its AI boom? Telecom tender offers clues
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 23:36:00
A technician conducts chip quality inspections in a factory in Yiwu, East China's Zhejiang Province, in March 2026. Photo: VCG Can China's homegrown technology stand up to the demands of its expanding artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure? According to media outlet CWW, China Telecom issued a tender recently for equipment for its 2026 intelligent computing supernode clusters. The project offers a real-world test of how far China's AI computing capabilities have advanced. As China's AI industry expands, its telecom operators are stepping up investment in computing infrastructure, with supernodes becoming an increasingly important part of the country's intelligent computing architecture. China Telecom explained in a 2025 article that a supernode combines AI chips housed in multiple servers into a large computing unit through high-speed interconnects. International debate over whether US chips and technology are being used in China's AI development has intensified in recent weeks. Rather than give credence to unsubstantiated speculation, a more grounded assessment should focus on what is actually being deployed in China's AI infrastructure, which companies are supplying the equipment and technologies, and how well their products perform in real-world applications. China Telecom's procurement could offer a glimpse of what is actually happening on the ground in China's AI industry. According to CWW, the tender covers an estimated 5,248 intelligent computing servers, among other equipment. It calls for two server configurations and sets high technical thresholds for GPU computing power and other performance parameters, with the systems designed to handle computationally intensive workloads such as large-language model training and high-concurrency inference. The tender allows for up to five suppliers to win contracts. Whoever they are, the procurement process offers a window into a broader reality: China's AI infrastructure development is far from opaque. This is not unique to China Telecom. Many Chinese companies publicly disclose procurement notices and bidding procedures, giving outside observers ample information to understand how the country's AI infrastructure is being built. The information is there for anyone willing to look. Yet some overseas commentators seem determined to look the other way, continuing to speculate about China's so-called dependence on US chips, or even claiming that it has resorted to smuggling them. Such narratives reveal little about China's AI development, but far more about the arrogance of those advancing them and the political agendas they serve. So, can China's homegrown chips support the development of its AI industry? There is no shortage of real-world examples. At an intelligent computing center in Wuxi, East China's Jiangsu Province, 2,000 units of the Moore Threads MTT S5000 are now running close to full capacity. Designed for generative AI workloads, the MTT S5000 is a full-featured GPU accelerator for large-language model training, inference and high-performance computing, powered by Moore Threads' next-generation PH100 chip. China's AI industry is expanding at a remarkable pace, requiring enormous quantities of chips to power its growth. Does anyone seriously believe that an industry developing on this scale could be powered by "smuggled US chips?" The notion is not just implausible; it is frankly absurd. Anyone making such claims seems to have little understanding of the sheer scale of China's AI development. China's drive for technological self-reliance is making steady progress. The rapid expansion of its AI infrastructure and the development of domestic large-language models show that homegrown chips are increasingly capable of supporting the country's AI industry. The most reliable way to assess China's technological capabilities is to look at what companies are actually buying, which suppliers are winning contracts and how their products perform in real-world applications. These facts offer far more insight than speculation abroad driven by political agendas. China's AI industry is still evolving, and so is its homegrown chip sector. China Telecom's latest tender points to the scale of demand emerging in the market. That demand means more orders, more revenue for research and development and stronger incentives for suppliers to improve their products. As China's AI industry grows, it is also creating the market conditions for its homegrown chipmakers to advance.

item.title: Xi welcomes Trump, meets Putin and Lee as APEC diplomacy gathers pace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 23:36:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, pose for a group photo with leaders and representatives from APEC economies and their spouses in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province on November 18, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday had a series of bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, following a packed diplomatic schedule on Tuesday. Chinese experts said the meetings highlight the role of head-of-state diplomacy in guiding bilateral relations, managing differences and strengthening mutual trust. With international attention focused on Shenzhen, this major event of China's diplomacy as a host offers an opportunity to advance multilateral cooperation and bring greater stability to a changing and turbulent world. Diplomacy as host setting direction Xi welcomed US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport. Amid welcome music, Xi and Trump shook hands warmly. Honor guards of the Chinese People's Liberation Army presented arms to salute, and a girl handed the US leader a bouquet, the Xinhua News Agency reported. The national flags of China and the US fluttered in the wind as a military band played the national anthems of the two countries, and fighter jets flew overhead in salute. The two heads of state waved to a welcoming young crowd. Xi recalled his state visit to the US in September this year, when the US presidential couple came to the airport in person and hosted a grand welcome ceremony, noting that China is a nation with a tradition of courtesy that values reciprocating goodwill, according to Xinhua. Extending his welcome to Trump for visiting China again, Xi said that he looks forward to conducting in-depth exchanges with the US president on major issues concerning bilateral relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape to advance a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. Trump thanked Xi for greeting him in person at the airport and for the special arrangements by the Chinese side. He said it is a great pleasure to visit China again, calling China a great country and Xi a great leader. Trump said that every meeting with Xi had been very pleasant, and he believes that the visit will further advance bilateral relations and achieve complete success, according to Xinhua. Earlier on Wednesday, Xi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin, during which Xi said China-Russia relations have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence and transformation, Xinhua reported. Xi called on both countries to deepen all-round cooperation and firmly uphold the due responsibilities and obligations of major countries to guide and promote a multipolar world and democratization of international relations. The development of China and Russia is closely intertwined with that of the Asia-Pacific region, and APEC is an important platform for enhancing cooperation. China stands ready to work with the Asia-Pacific family, including Russia, to chart a course for the region's prosperity and development and build an Asia-Pacific community together, Xi said. Putin said he and Xi have held four productive meetings so far this year, helping sustain the sound development momentum in Russia-China relations. High-level exchanges have been close, bilateral trade has reached a new high, and practical cooperation has made substantial progress across various fields, he said. Russia is willing to strengthen back-to-back strategic coordination with China, expand cooperation in trade, energy, education and other fields, and broaden cultural and people-to-people exchanges to better benefit the two peoples, Putin said. Zhang Hong, a research fellow at the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, described China-Russia relations as an example of how major countries can work together while accommodating differences. The two countries pursue partnership without forming an alliance, cooperate where their interests converge and refrain from interfering in each other's internal affairs. Continued coordination on geopolitical security issues has also helped them build firm mutual trust, he said. Xi on Wednesday also called for advancing the steady and sound development of relations between China and the Republic of Korea (ROK) as next year marks the 35th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two "friendly neighbors and strategic cooperative partners" during his meeting with ROK President Lee Jae-myung, Xinhua reported. The two countries should uphold strategic independence, maintain the political foundation for bilateral relations, and further consolidate and develop the relationship, Xi stressed. China and the ROK have substantially concluded the second phase of negotiations on the China-ROK Free Trade Agreement. The two countries should make full use of this institutional arrangement to strengthen macroeconomic policy coordination and foster a collaborative ecosystem for emerging technology industries such as artificial intelligence, Xi said. For his part, Lee said that the two countries have seen sustained momentum in the comprehensive restoration of ROK-China relations, with bilateral economic and trade cooperation growing rapidly, people-to-people exchanges becoming increasingly frequent, and mutual perceptions steadily improving, according to Xinhua. The ROK's commitment to the one-China policy has not changed and will not change, Lee stressed. The two leaders had met in Beijing in January during Lee's China visit as well as during last year's APEC meeting in South Korea. The Shenzhen summit provided an important platform for the Chinese and South Korean leaders to meet again and set new goals for bilateral relations and economic ties, Lü Chao, an expert on Northeast Asian affairs at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times on Wednesday. Their shared support for free trade and multilateral cooperation provides an important basis for further engagement, Lü said. Stronger relations reflect both countries' aspirations, the efforts of their leaders and the need to build a Northeast Asian community, he added. Bilateral engagement draws global attention International coverage highlights both the significance of the encounters and expectations for closer cooperation. International reporting also highlights expectations for stable relations and practical cooperation. Reuters reported on Wednesday that "most analysts expect Washington and Beijing to keep ties relatively stable," despite continuing trade and technology frictions. South Korea's The Korea Herald highlighted the potential economic benefits of closer bilateral engagement. In its coverage of Wednesday's summit, the newspaper said a successful agreement on services and investment "stands to benefit South Korean businesses seeking greater access to China's market," identifying tourism, gaming, entertainment and other service industries as potential beneficiaries. Singapore's CNA, in a report published on Tuesday, also highlighted the importance of bilateral diplomacy alongside the multilateral agenda. "Their own side meetings with other leaders are as important to them as the attention-grabbing great-power dialogues," Drew Thompson, a senior fellow at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, told CNA. These expectations reflect opportunities that countries see in engaging with China, Wang Yiwei, a professor at the School of International Studies at Renmin University of China, told the Global Times on Wednesday, noting that China's diplomacy as a host has become a distinctive feature of its major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics in the new era, underpinned by a more proactive approach to opening-up and sharing development opportunities with the world. China is advancing unilateral opening-up and institutional opening-up, Wang said. Its industrial capacity and position in global industrial, supply and value chains provide a material foundation for cooperation, with opportunities spanning agriculture, manufacturing and the digital economy. That breadth of opportunity helps explain why more countries are seeking closer engagement with China, he said. Rising populism in some countries and uncertainty about external support are also encouraging countries to come to China for dialogue and cooperation. China's diplomacy as a host consistently advocates true multilateralism and open regionalism. Shenzhen offers visitors a view of China's development and of possibilities for wider global cooperation. As existing approaches struggle to address global challenges, the city's experience of innovation and opening-up offers inspirations for exploring new paths, the expert stressed.

item.title: Xi calls for jointly building Asia-Pacific community to prosper together
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 22:36:00
Chinese President Xi Jinping delivers a keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 at the Qianhai International Convention Center in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Photo: Xinhua) Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, on Wednesday hosted a banquet in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, to welcome guests who are here to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting. Openness is deeply rooted in Shenzhen's DNA and innovation drives the city's vitality, while cooperation is where its strength comes from, Xi said in his toast, adding that the success of Shenzhen is also a microcosm of China's reform and opening-up, as well as an example of fruitful cooperation across the Asia-Pacific, the Xinhua News Agency reported. Noting that openness, innovation and cooperation have been the distinctive features of APEC since its establishment, Xi said APEC has grasped the pulse of the times and guided the process of regional economic integration, making the Asia-Pacific the most dynamic region and a vital growth engine of the world economy. "At the economic leaders' meeting tomorrow, we will discuss measures to expand two-way opening up, explore paths of innovation-driven growth and unfold more opportunities of practical cooperation in various fields," Xi said. Amid uncertainties facing global economic growth and the rise of trade protectionism and unilateralism, this year's APEC meeting provides an important platform for economies to strengthen communication and deepen cooperation. China's call for building an Asia-Pacific community and promoting common prosperity not only focuses on regional economic growth, but also offers ideas for economies at different stages of development to explore open, inclusive and mutually beneficial cooperation, Chinese observers said. Bridging the divides Xi on Wednesday also delivered a keynote speech at the APEC CEO Summit 2026. This year, China is hosting APEC for the third time. We are ready to work with all other parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and bring prosperity for all in our region, Xi said, according to Xinhua. The speech once again demonstrated China's thinking on addressing current challenges facing the global economy, offering a new approach to cooperation through the building of an open Asia-Pacific economy, Liu Guohong, president of the China Development Institute, told the Global Times on Wednesday. The key to the regional cooperation advocated by China, Liu said, lies in respecting the different development stages and institutional characteristics of individual economies, and finding pathways for common development through equal consultation. In his speech, Xi also said China supports the establishment of a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges and interactions among bay areas from across the world. This will help us explore new ways for stronger economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. Citing the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), Liu explained how cities with different institutional systems and levels of development can coexist while advancing regional integration. He noted that economies at different stages of development and with different institutional characteristics inevitably encounter various obstacles and challenges, but the neutral nature of technology could help reduce barriers to cross-regional flows. "APEC economies shall use the inclusive benefits of technology to break through the predicament facing the region, achieve coexistence while seeking common ground, and realize shared prosperity through inclusive development," Liu said. This reflects a broader approach to regional cooperation: cooperation should not be conditional on economies having identical development levels or institutional systems. Instead, inclusive arrangements should allow all parties to participate, Liu added. Foreign business representatives also offered their perspectives on the cooperation proposals and opportunities in China. In a lounge area opposite the conference venue, Global Times reporters saw business representatives engaging in lively discussions about the APEC CEO Summit. In interviews with the Global Times at the summit, many highlighted the importance of the Chinese market, while several expressed particular appreciation for the emphasis on people-centered development and openness in the Chinese president's keynote speech. Saravoot Yoovidhya, CEO of Thailand's TCP Group, told the Global Times that China's continued opening-up offers global investors broad opportunities and a predictable environment. Arnaud Favry, head of APAC Government Affairs and Policy, told the Global Times China could play an important role in integrating Asian economies into a broader regional community. He stressed that in terms of innovation, China is really leading the pack. It would be beneficial for foreign actors to join forces with Chinese players to tackle the world market. Joanna Kay, program director of International Strategy, Partnerships and Engagement, emphasized that economic development should be people-centered, bringing more countries and communities into conversation and allowing them to share development experiences. Regional economic growth can truly benefit society only when communities, families and ordinary people are placed at its center, she told the Global Times. The experience accumulated by the GBA in trade and investment, industrial cooperation and connectivity among cities could offer a reference for Asia-Pacific economies seeking to deepen cooperation. We are not afraid of competition. Rather, we hope the Asia-Pacific can move toward a future that provides people with a better and happier life, said Xiao Geng, Professor at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen), also Director of the Institute of Policy and Practice at the Shenzhen Finance Institute. The ultimate value of regional cooperation lies not only in expanding trade and investment, but also in bringing innovation into the real economy, translating growth into tangible fruits that can ensure the benefits of development reach ordinary people, he said. Participants exchange views outside the venue as the opening ceremony of the 2026 APEC CEO Summit is held in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province on November 18, 2026. Photo: Xinhua Vision into action This year marks the start of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) for economic and social development. A blueprint for China's development, the 15th Five-Year Plan also provides a list of opportunities for promoting economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and the wider world, Xi noted in the keynote speech. China will provide the global business community with its super-large, open market, broad development prospects, as well as a cooperative environment that promotes mutual progress, said the Chinese president. The call for greater opportunities and open market also resonated in the remarks of other leaders at the APEC CEO Summit, with discussions highlighting the importance of keeping markets open and strengthening economic ties amid global uncertainty. The APEC CEO Summit Shenzhen Initiative 2026 was released on Wednesday. This marks the first time in the 30-year history of the summit that an outcome document has been issued in the form of an initiative. According to Xinhua, the initiative states that, guided by four priority areas - openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven growth, greater connectivity and mutually beneficial cooperation - the Asia-Pacific business community stands ready to work with all economies to fully implement the Putrajaya Vision 2040 and build an open, dynamic, resilient and peaceful Asia-Pacific community. It also calls for translating this year's APEC theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," into concrete actions, so that the Asia-Pacific region continues to serve as the world's most dynamic engine of growth and a community of shared prosperity. Xiao noted that a longstanding challenge for the APEC platform is how to keep its members united and going forward further. Historically, it has lacked outcome documents with strong implementability. The Shenzhen Initiative addresses a structural gap within APEC as a voluntary cooperation mechanism, seeking to build a trackable and accountable framework for future cooperation. It systematically incorporates business community input on connectivity, an AI innovation ecosystem, the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP), the digital economy and sustainable development. Presented to the Economic Leaders' Meeting, it serves as an "anchor for consensus" to guide follow-up cooperation, Xiao added. Zhou Xing, vice chairman and public affairs managing partner at PwC China, told the Global Times that as fragmented rules and inconsistent standards are raising compliance costs for businesses and undermining the region's overall competitiveness, what the Asia-Pacific business community expects most is certainty. Businesses are particularly concerned about whether measurable progress can be made in areas such as trade facilitation, the digital economy, green transformation and supply chain resilience. Consensus reached through APEC meeting should also be translated into concrete projects, cooperation platforms and channels for business participation, Zhou said.

item.title: China's trade with APEC economies accounts for over 60% of total foreign trade, underpins stability: experts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 22:01:00
A section of Shennan Boulevard, a major traffic artery in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, is decorated by flowers on November 11, 2026 as the city is gearing up to host the APEC meetings. Photo: VCG China's trade with other Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) economies surged 25.4 percent year-on-year to 27.08 trillion yuan ($4.06 trillion) in the first 10 months of 2026, accounting for 60.4 percent of the country's total foreign trade, according to data released by the General Administration of Customs (GAC) on Wednesday. Chinese experts said the figures underscore the Asia-Pacific region's pivotal role in China's foreign trade, with closer regional economic ties providing a solid foundation for trade growth and strengthening the resilience of regional supply chains. The growth rate was 5.4 percentage points higher than China's overall foreign trade growth during the period, while the share of trade with other APEC economies increased by 2.6 percentage points from a year earlier, according to the GAC. China's exports to other APEC economies rose 22.6 percent year-on-year, while imports increased 29.1 percent, outpacing export growth by 6.5 percentage points, according to the GAC. "APEC economies are a crucial pillar of China's foreign trade," Liang Haiming, president of the Belt and Road Research Institute at Hainan University and head of the Silk Road iValley Research Institute, told the Global Times on Wednesday. "With other APEC economies accounting for 60.4 percent of China's total foreign trade, the Asia-Pacific region occupies a crucial position in the country's trade landscape. Maintaining stable economic and trade relations across the region is essential to safeguarding the fundamentals of China's foreign trade," Liang said. China's trade with 14 of the other 20 APEC economies recorded double-digit growth in the first 10 months, with imports and exports with South Korea, Vietnam and Peru each expanding by more than 30 percent, according to the GAC. Ningbo offers a tangible example of the broader trend reflected in the data released by the GAC. According to Ningbo Customs, the city's trade with other APEC economies reached 705.98 billion yuan in the January-October period, up 10 percent year-on-year. Exports rose 14.3 percent to 458.87 billion yuan, while imports increased 2.9 percent to 247.11 billion yuan. Major imports included bulk commodities and mechanical and electrical products, while exports included mechanical and electrical products and labor-intensive goods. Wang Xiaodong, head of a Ningbo-based metal products company, said the firm had established a factory in Vietnam at an early stage and continued to optimize its cost structure by leveraging the institutional advantages of trade facilitation under the APEC framework. "In the first 10 months, we imported 31.995 million yuan worth of intermediate goods, including connecting rods and standard sockets, from Vietnam, up 63.3 percent year-on-year," Wang said. Another Ningbo-based company has also seen the benefits of cooperation during 2026 APEC "China Year," with orders from APEC economies including Mexico and Indonesia continuing to rise and production schedules already extending into 2027. Chen Shuhui, general manager of the company's overseas resources center, said its exports of elevators and other products to APEC economies reached nearly 90 million yuan in the first 10 months, an increase of more than 20 percent year-on-year. Liang said both the customs figures and the experiences of individual businesses reflect tangible achievements in regional cooperation and development, while demonstrating the solid market foundations of an Asia-Pacific community. He noted that China is playing an increasingly diversified role in Asia-Pacific supply chains through the APEC mechanism, extending beyond its traditional role as the "world's factory" to become the "world's market," a regional production hub and a platform for innovation and the application of new technologies. "These diversified roles have improved the overall efficiency of Asia-Pacific supply chains, lowered the costs of regional coordination and business cooperation, and strengthened the resilience of supply chains across the region, making them more stable and efficient," Liang said. The GAC said closer economic and trade ties between China and other APEC economies, supported by an open and interconnected regional market, have deepened mutually beneficial cooperation and injected fresh momentum into global economic growth.

item.title: Shenzhen APEC: an opportunity for Taiwan region to rediscover Chinese mainland
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 21:32:00
This photo taken on November 16, 2026 shows a view of Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province with APEC elements. China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. Photo: VCG Some local news coverage in Taiwan region often portrays the Chinese mainland as being in a state of "economic collapse." Yet along the Pearl River in Shenzhen, bright lights stream across the skyline and traffic flows nonstop, embodying a city brimming with innovative vitality. Both refer to the same Chinese mainland. Why, then, are the pictures so strikingly different? A remark made during a cross-Straits media program held around the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen is worth reflecting on. In a dialogue, Su Heng, Chairperson of the Cross-Straits Economic and Trade Exchange Association, shared her first visit to the Pearl River waterfront, where she saw a bustling, prosperous scene. She noted a stark contrast: back home in Taiwan region, mainstream reports repeatedly claim that the mainland's economy is "collapsing." Why is there such a stark difference? Taiwan journalists covering APEC in Shenzhen offer a clear lens to examine this information gap. Reporters from China Times and United Daily News documented life scenes in the city, from robots making coffee to drones delivering takeout. Autonomous taxis could be seen navigating the streets, while service robots were a common sight. In Shenzhen, technologies once confined to laboratories are being transformed into practical applications that are increasingly accessible to ordinary people. However, audiences in Taiwan do not always receive the same story. Some "pan-green" media outlets disparaged Shenzhen's cityscape and focused on reports of robots malfunctioning. This contrast reflects Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' manipulation of public opinion. Taiwan singer and songwriter Lo Ta-yu criticized the DPP authorities in a recent radio interview, saying they had become a source of fear among Taiwan residents and are contributing to a decline in the island's cultural environment. His remarks have sparked widespread discussion on both sides of the Taiwan Straits. Chen Binhua, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated clearly that the DPP authorities push "cultural Taiwan independence" for political gain, creating "green terror" and a chilling effect. These actions hurt the interests of Taiwan compatriots and spark widespread discontent. The truth is not allowed to be heard because the DPP fears Taiwan residents will embrace joint development with the mainland. As Zhang Wensheng, deputy dean and a professor at the Taiwan Research Institute of Xiamen University, told the Global Times, "pan‑green media and commentators have long smeared the mainland, portraying it as backward and closed. This narrative feeds the false sense of superiority held by 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces, built on biased imagination." Such superiority, founded on distortion and lies, collapses when faced with real‑world facts. Cooperation opportunities abound, while the authorities keep erecting cognitive barriers. This contradiction also shows in Taiwan authorities' APEC arrangements. Lai Ching-te once again sent Stan Shih, who represented Taiwan's authorities at APEC in 2007, to this year's summit with three "mandates": participate actively in APEC affairs, advance global tech cooperation, and deepen ties with key partners. These priorities center on tech and AI supply chains. In essence, they seek to coordinate with the US to compete against the Chinese mainland in supply chains, attaching Taiwan region to Washington in APEC. However, reliance on outside forces will only marginalize Taiwan within this regional framework. The language is all about "cooperation," but behind it lies a political calculation to pursue "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces. Against this backdrop, some commentators in Taiwan region have lamented that many people on the island increasingly feel like outsiders. The Chinese mainland's vast market and innovation momentum are within reach, yet Taiwan region's public is intentionally kept away from this development arena by DPP. Taiwan region's businesspeople who came to Shenzhen for APEC have simple, practical hopes: capture gains from the mainland's high‑quality growth. Ordinary people want to work together, but the DPP authorities keep building barriers and stoking confrontation. The mainland has opened far more than just the window of this Shenzhen APEC meeting for Taiwan compatriots. It has opened the door for shared growth and mutual progress - and that door stays open. Opportunity waits right outside. Why should all Taiwan compatriots be shut out just to serve the political interests of a select few?

item.title: Several Chinese chipmakers post upbeat Q3 earnings as homegrown computing push gains momentum
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 18:26:00
A technician conducts chip quality inspections in a factory in Yiwu, East China's Zhejiang Province, in March 2026. Photo: VCG China's leading artificial intelligence (AI) and memory chipmakers have reported a string of strong third-quarter results, underscoring how surging demand for computing power and tighter US export controls are accelerating the country's drive toward greater semiconductor self-sufficiency. As geopolitical uncertainty is driving users toward Chinese chips and developers are now shifting their focus to compatibility layers for domestic alternatives, industry analysts said on Wednesday that the latest earnings and shipment data suggest China's semiconductor sector is moving beyond merely accelerating import substitution and increasing autonomy across the industrial chain, toward a more system-level form of competition. China's leading memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) reported 118.71 billion yuan ($17.80 billion) in revenue for the third quarter of 2026, marking a 19 percent quarter-on-quarter increase and a massive 613.2 percent year-on-year surge. President and CEO Cao Kanyu said at the company's third-quarter earnings briefing on Tuesday that the increase was driven by higher production capacity, faster ramp-up at its wafer fabs and stronger pricing in the dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) market amid a supply shortage since 2025. According to Cao, the company's three 12-inch wafer fabs had seen steadily improving utilization, helping lower unit fixed costs, while process maturity and yield gains had reduced manufacturing costs further. He added that the company had signed long-term supply agreements with several major customers to secure medium- to long-term demand visibility. Industry observers said that CXMT's performance reflects broader momentum across China's semiconductor supply chain, where demand expansion and domestic substitution are both supporting growth. Market sentiment around domestic AI chips also improved after recent concerns over the Nvidia CEO's controversy. On Wednesday, shares linked to AI computing rose in early trading, with Huadong Heavy Machinery Co extending its rally to a fourth consecutive limit-up session. Other stocks including Moore Threads, Cambricon Technology, Hygon Information Technology, MetaX and Loongson Technology also gained. The rally comes as Chinese chipmakers continue to post faster growth. MetaX said at an earnings call on Monday that it is focusing on providing GPU computing platforms for Chinese customers and strengthening local supply chain compatibility. The company reported revenue of 1.5 billion yuan for July-September, up 367 percent from a year earlier. Meanwhile, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp's third-quarter revenue hit a record $3.19 billion, up 6.1 percent quarter-on-quarter. Moore Threads said its third-quarter revenue jumped 1,773.92 percent year-on-year to 1.55 billion yuan, a record high. The gains come against a backdrop of explosive demand for AI computing. China's AI computing centers are being built out at a faster pace, and domestic chips are gaining traction in both training and inference workloads, said analysts at China Securities Co. The progression of AI applications from proof of concept to practical use in specific industries, together with exponential growth in annual recurring revenue from AI models and token volumes, is keeping the sector in a high-growth phase, they added, 21jingji.com reported. According to a TrendForce forecast cited by Chinese media outlets on Wednesday, China's shipments of high-end AI chips are expected to reach 5 million units in 2026, up 83 percent from a year earlier. A separate IDC report cited by Reuters showed Nvidia's share of China's data-center AI chip market fell to 34 percent in the first half of 2026, as US export controls constrained supply and domestic rivals led by Huawei gained ground. Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators in China in the January-to-June period, down 44 percent from a year earlier, while Huawei shipped 572,000 units, taking a 28 percent market share. Alibaba's chip-design unit T-Head held 7 percent, followed by Cambricon Technology with 5 percent, Baidu's Kunlunxin with 4 percent and Hygon Information Technology with 3 percent, according to the IDC report. From a global perspective, the mismatch between supply and demand is creating room for domestic players to expand. In the first half of 2026, the global AI chip market was worth about 1.39 trillion yuan, up more than 80 percent year on year, according to a report by Dadao Times Think Tank. The US accounted for about 94 percent of supply, while China represented only 6 percent, despite being the world's second-largest AI chip market and accounting for an estimated 20 percent to 30 percent of demand. "Competition was shifting from the performance of a single chip to system-level capabilities, including how well chips work in a larger computing cluster," Tian Feng, president of the Fast Think Institute and former dean of the Intelligence Industry Research Institute at SenseTime, told the Global Times on Wednesday. Tian said the industry is moving from a phase focused on filling gaps caused by external restrictions to one centered on scaling, efficiency and ecosystem building, noting that the key battleground is no longer just whether domestic chips can replace foreign ones, but whether they can compete on cost performance, delivery capability and system efficiency. That transition is already visible in China's rapidly expanding domestic AI infrastructure. In July, the fully domestic 100,000-card AI supercluster "Sugon 8000 (Dengfeng)" was officially launched and put into operation, using Chinese-designed chips, computing systems, storage and networking components. It marks the country's first AI supercluster capable of supporting over 100,000 domestically developed computing cards, said its developer Sugon Information Industry Co. However, analysts caution that China's AI chip sector must overcome several major hurdles before it can achieve true autonomy. These include gaps between domestic and leading overseas solutions in top-end single-chip performance and software ecosystems, as well as the costs of adapting models, operators and scheduling systems when migrating across vendors. High-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging and manufacturing capacity also remain constraints on output and delivery speed. Even so, Tian said the combination of rising AI demand, heavy R&D spending and policy support is pushing China's domestic chip industry into a new phase, one in which the focus is shifting from "replaceability" to industrialization, scale and commercialization.

item.title: China prepares Shenzhou-24 mission to carry first Pakistani astronaut to space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 16:57:00
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spacecraft and its Long March-2F Y24 carrier rocket are transferred to the launch area at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center on November 17, 2026. The mission is scheduled to be launched in the coming days, following pre-launch checks and joint tests. Photo: VCG Preparations for the upcoming Shenzhou-24 crewed mission are progressing smoothly, with winter-proofing measures, upgraded launch facilities and a backup rescue system in place as China readies for a historic joint spaceflight that will see a Pakistani astronaut become the first foreign national to visit the China Space Station. The spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket are currently in good condition, and launch site facilities and equipment are operating normally, according to a release the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) provided to the Global Times on Tuesday. The spacecraft is scheduled for launch at an appropriate time, according to the CMSA release. The nearly 60-meter-tall spacecraft-rocket combination traveled approximately 1.5 kilometers along a seamless railway track during a vertical transfer that lasted about 90 minutes, according to China Media Group (CMG). As preparations enter their final stage, engineers at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in Northwest China's Gobi Desert are addressing the challenges posed by cold weather and conducting functional inspections and joint testing ahead of liftoff. The launch center has also introduced equipment upgrades to improve operational reliability. Nearly 20 voltage stabilization devices have been installed on the launch tower to ensure a more stable electricity supply during propellant loading and launch operations, while propellant filling pumps that had been in service for more than two decades have been replaced, the state broadcaster revealed. Meanwhile, a separate spacecraft-rocket combination is already standing by as part of China's emergency rescue arrangements for crewed space missions. The Long March-2F Y25 rocket and Shenzhou-25 spacecraft have been placed on standby inside the vertical assembly building, space expert Yang Yuguang noted when interviewed by the state broadcaster. Should an emergency arise involving the Shenzhou-24 crew in orbit, the backup system is designed to enable rapid testing and transfer of the rescue spacecraft and rocket, allowing China to launch an emergency rescue mission within a relatively short period, according to CMG. Pang Zhihao, a Beijing-based senior space expert, told the Global Times on Wednesday that the preparations demonstrate the comprehensive safety measures supporting the mission, while the successful transfer of the spacecraft and rocket provides an important foundation for subsequent joint testing and functional checks. The temperature at the launch site is expected to be around 1 C during the transfer, with northwesterly winds, according to the CMG report on Wednesday. Pang said that the preparations are supported by a combination of passive thermal insulation and active heating measures designed to protect the rocket and spacecraft from low temperatures. The launch tower is equipped with enclosed protective structures and heating systems that continuously supply temperature-controlled air to the rocket's fairing and body, while insulation materials are applied to critical components, Pang explained. Additional temperature-control systems are installed around propellant tanks and engine components to ensure that sensitive equipment remains within appropriate operating ranges. "The launch procedures have also been optimized to delay the opening of the tower's rotating platforms and minimize the time the rocket and spacecraft are exposed to low temperatures," Pang told the Global Times. These measures, along with real-time meteorological monitoring and contingency plans for extreme cold, are intended to prevent temperature-related abnormalities in electronic components and propellants, ensuring the safety and reliability of the launch, he said. A Pakistani astronaut is expected to participate in the mission as a payload specialist and will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after completing a short-term stay in orbit. The Pakistani astronaut will be the first foreign astronaut to step into China's space station, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun highlighted during a regular press conference on November 9. This marks yet another key outcome of bilateral cooperation as the two countries mark the 75th anniversary of China-Pakistan diplomatic ties, he noted. Looking ahead to the upcoming mission, Pang expressed hope that Shenzhou-24 would achieve a successful launch and safe in-orbit operations, with Chinese and foreign astronauts working closely together to carry out scientific experiments and extravehicular activities. He also voiced expectations that the Pakistani payload specialist would successfully conduct scientific research aboard the China Space Station. "The mission is expected to yield valuable scientific data and open a new chapter in international cooperation aboard the China Space Station, as China continues to embrace an open and collaborative approach to exploring the vast universe," Pang told the Global Times. Adding a human dimension to this historic mission, both Pakistani astronauts shortlisted for the mission have previously studied Chinese at the Confucius Institute in Islamabad, according to a recent report published by China News Service. Qu Zhaowei, Secretary of the Party Committee of Beijing Language and Culture University, revealed the information in an exclusive interview with China News Service on November 13 during the 2026 World Chinese Language Conference. "Both astronauts previously studied Chinese at the Confucius Institute in Islamabad," Qu said. Describing their journey from Chinese language classrooms to the prospect of traveling into space as both meaningful and inspiring, Qu said the experience demonstrates how Chinese is increasingly becoming a bridge connecting knowledge, technology, innovation and humanity's future. Qu noted that language proficiency is particularly important in highly specialized fields such as aerospace, where accurately understanding technical concepts, professional instructions and operational procedures is essential. The two candidates' experience reflects how Chinese language education is expanding beyond everyday communication into increasingly sophisticated areas of international scientific and technological cooperation, he said.

item.title: Shenzhen residents put their best foot forward to welcome APEC as related hashtag tops Weibo trending list
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 15:41:00
Shenzhen resident Xiaoxi posts on social media, calling on fellow residents to swap their usual flip-flops for sneakers during APEC week to present a more polished image of the city. Photo: Screenshot from website The hashtag "Shenzhen residents dress up to welcome APEC" topped the trending list on China's X-like social media platform Sina Weibo on Wednesday, sparking widespread discussion as the APEC week got underway in the southern Chinese city. With colorful flags lining the roads, flowers brightening the streets and buses and metro trains sporting new looks, Shenzhen has been getting "dressed up" for the international gathering. And its residents are getting into host mode, too - some quite literally by changing their shoes. Residents wearing white sneakers are seen at Qianhai Stone Park near the Qianhai International Conference Center in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong Province, during APEC week. Photo: Screenshot from website In South China's Guangdong Province, however, flip-flops are more than just casual footwear. They are a familiar part of everyday life. From office workers to business executives, many locals slip out of their formal shoes and into sandals once they settle into the office. The familiar slap-slap sound of flip-flops on the streets is almost part of the region's everyday soundtrack. The preference has practical roots. Guangdong's subtropical and tropical climate brings long, hot and humid periods, along with frequent rainfall. Flip-flops offer ventilation in the heat and are convenient in wet weather. Over time, they have come to represent more than mere comfort, embodying the laid-back lifestyle that many people in Guangdong cherish. Against this backdrop, some Shenzhen residents have decided to put their flip-flops aside for APEC week. "I'm giving up flip-flops this week to welcome APEC!" As the meeting week began, some residents took to social media to say they were swapping their signature casual footwear for clean, comfortable sneakers, hoping to present a more polished image of the city to visiting guests. One resident, who goes by the online name Xiaoxi, had urged fellow residents online to reconsider their footwear for the occasion. Having worn flip-flops throughout the year, she decided to put them aside during APEC week. "What if someone takes photos of Shenzhen's cityscape and I happen to appear in one of them as a passer-by? I'd like to present a better image," she told Jimu News. She bought a new pair of sneakers to mark the occasion and even put on makeup before heading out on Tuesday, despite rarely wearing it to work. Although she is not originally from Shenzhen, Xiaoxi has lived and built her career in the city for nearly a decade. She said this small change to her everyday habits was her way of embracing her role as a host and contributing to the city. Her post prompted lively reactions online. One user said they rarely wore sneakers but had dug out a pair of white ones they had bought two years earlier when visiting the Qianhai Museum on November 15. Others said they would also switch from flip-flops to sneakers after seeing the post. Across social media, residents shared their own takes on the footwear trend. Some showed off their carefully styled Crocs, others planned to wear white sneakers, while a few said they would opt for heeled shoes to mark the occasion. But not everyone was ready to give up their flip-flops, with some saying they would stick to their usual relaxed style. "The contrast between those choosing to dress up and those sticking to their flip-flops is not a matter of right or wrong. Rather, it reflects the diversity and inclusiveness of Shenzhen, where residents have found different ways to express their enthusiasm for hosting the international event," a Shenzhen resident surnamed Su said. Notably, no one has required residents to change how they dress. These gestures have emerged spontaneously, reflecting resident's personal sense of belonging and willingness to take part in welcoming visitors. The relevant topic of "Shenzhen residents dress up to welcome APEC" has gained more than 66 million of views on Weibo as of press time on Wednesday. Xie Kexin, a Shenzhen native who has long worked in the international education sector, told the Global Times that APEC provides an important platform for dialogue and cooperation across the Asia-Pacific. "The city's carefully prepared streetscapes, efficient transport system and modern venues offer one glimpse of Shenzhen to the world, but the attitudes and everyday choices of its residents provide another, more personal window into the city," she said. "Together, the polished sneakers and relaxed flip-flops make up a distinctly Shenzhen welcome," Xie said. "The city's residents are showing the world that hospitality does not mean giving up their everyday character. Shenzhen is ready to welcome international guests with warmth and sincerity, while remaining confident in its openness and diversity."

item.title: Hong Kong's AI-powered surveillance camera network also safeguards national security, personal data protected, police force tells GT
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-18 11:35:00
Picture of Hong Kong street. Photo: VCG The Hong Kong Police Force told the Global Times on Wednesday that the city's AI-powered surveillance camera network was designed not only to prevent and investigate crime but also to safeguard national security, maintain public order and protect lives and property. Meanwhile, the police force stressed in a statement that personal data collected through the SmartView network would be kept only as long as necessary for its intended purpose, and for no more than six months, following the activation of facial recognition technology across the network on Monday. Beyond criminal investigations, facial recognition technology could also help locate missing persons, including children lost in large crowds, allowing officers to identify and find them more quickly and accurately, according to the statement. The police force said the AI features of the SmartView system would serve only as investigative tools, helping officers sift through and analyze surveillance footage more efficiently and freeing them to focus on other police work. The force emphasized that any information flagged by the system would still be subject to human review and assessment, with officers relying on other investigative methods before deciding on further action, as they do under existing procedures. Launched in 2024, the SmartView network is a Hong Kong regional government-led initiative to expand surveillance across the city, with cameras installed to help combat crime and safeguard national security. Police have deployed more than 10,000 cameras so far and plan to increase that number to 60,000 by 2028. The cameras are mounted on ordinary and smart lampposts, government buildings and police vehicles. Authorities have also announced plans to connect the network to surveillance systems in shopping malls this year. In response to public concerns about data security, the police force told the Global Times that access to the system's facial recognition features would be restricted to a small number of trained officers, who must obtain supervisory approval before each use. All operations would be logged and reviewed for compliance. Police said surveillance footage would be retained for no more than 31 days and facial recognition data for no more than 180 days, in accordance with the city's privacy laws.
